speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether the Ministry has received appeals from Singaporeans for help and subsidies to pay medical fees for their non-Singaporean relatives or foreign spouses in the past five years and if so, how many such cases there have been; and (b) whether the Ministry can work with ICA to consider implementing a policy requiring such foreign relatives or spouses visiting Singapore on long term visit pass to purchase medical insurance during their visit.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether the citizen-level subsidies for maternity fees accorded to foreign mothers giving birth to Singapore Citizens apply to all items incurred during a typical maternity hospitalisation or only to specified items; (b) if only for specified items, what are the specific items; and (c) whether a review will be done to equalise or reduce the disparity in the total bill size for all foreign mothers giving birth to Singapore Citizens.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about maternity hospitalisation subsidies accorded to foreign mothers giving birth to Singapore Citizens.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The majority of foreign spouses with Singapore Citizen children are Permanent Residents (PRs) or holders of Long-Term Visit Pass-Plus (LTVP+).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Therefore, they are eligible for healthcare subsidies in public healthcare institutions.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Ultimately, as healthcare subsidies are borne by all Singaporeans, any extension of these benefits to foreigners must be assessed carefully.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Foreigners facing financial difficulties with their healthcare bills may approach our medical social workers for assistance.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Healthcare insurance is another way to help protect families with foreigner members on LTVP or Dependant’s Pass from large hospital bills.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Today, such individuals may buy plans offered by Integrated Shield Plan insurers and pay premiums in cash or using their Singapore Citizen/PR family members’ MediSave.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have three supplementary questions for the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, I have asked for the figures from the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) for the answer to this, so I do not know, but does the Ministry of Health (MOH) also acknowledge that there is a significant number of Singaporean children being born to foreign mothers who are not holders of PR or LTVP+ but LTVP itself or less.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, if we look at the cost differential for foreign mothers giving birth to Singapore Citizens who are not holders of PR or LTVP+, does MOH not find that the total bill size is significantly higher than that for LTVP+ or PR mothers, in the sense that it works against our aim to increase our TFR, because the cost is just too high?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And finally, if we were to consider extending further support to this group of foreign mothers who are not PRs or LTVP+ holders, I think we are looking at probably a limited number of people and these delivery episodes are once in a lifetime, maybe twice.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, the majority of those who are foreign spouses, they are PRs or LTVP+ holders.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I would just highlight a couple of things to address the other questions that the Member has raised.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The concern is really the Singapore child and you are helping a Singaporean with this situation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It means that from the time they are admitted for delivery to the discharge of the mother after birth, it is fully covered at Singaporean rates.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In that sense, the issue of the Singaporean child not being supported, does not exist because for any mother who is delivering a Singaporean child and if they are a PR or LTVP+ holder, the whole episode of delivery is covered.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, if the mother is in the process of applying for her LTVP+ and it has not yet been approved, and she then got admitted but there is a process or an application pending, she can actually apply for the rates to be applicable to her as well.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is also something that addresses those concerns.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There are two other points I wanted to make.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, in that sense, they are also covered for some of their other expenses.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In any case, if there are any difficulties, the foreign spouses may also seek help from medical social workers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, actually, a large part of the concerns that the Member has are already addressed with the existing policies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But we will continue to look at all gaps.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We always review our financing policies regularly to see if there are emerging trends or needs that we need to address.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: One more supplementary question for the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: She mentioned in her answer that the number of foreign mothers giving birth to Singaporean children who are not already PRs or LTVP+ holders is small, less than 10%.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I think as she correctly acknowledged, we are all in this together.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Every Singaporean child born is precious to us.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, given that the numbers are not large, according to what the Ministry has just said, then I think there is scope for us to review, to see how we can better support, financially at least, the delivery episodes of these mothers who are holders of LTVP or less Passes.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As I mentioned, we will continue to assess this situation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But the Member may want to consider for those situations where the mother comes in, what they can do is to apply for LTVP+ and if she satisfies that requirement, she will then be entitled to Singapore Citizen rates.
